rv.q: In the BLO’s current production, Grammy Award-winning soprano Brittany Renee all but blows the roof off the Emerson Cutler Majestic with her powerfully pure vocals and a shatteringly on-point dramatic portrayal that eschews Blanche’s physical fragility and instead focuses on the emotional frailty deep within the character.
The production was a triumph in storytelling, its ending lingering with viewers long after the curtain fell.
Brightest among these was soprano Brittany Renee, who pulled the audience into her twisted dreams as Blanche DuBois, prompting a standing ovation for her company and role debut.

Ultimately, this production gives us the exact magic Tennessee Williams envisioned, and Previn so brilliantly scored.

cn.t: BLO's operatic *Streetcar* earns mostly praise for its cast and direction, though Previn's adaptation draws mixed reactions—some find it stunning, others see a libretto too tethered to the play to fully soar as opera.
